title: I Built N3ONDefense With AI — But the Game Design Is Mine
author: Thin_Alternative2372
selftext:
I’ve been building **N3ONDefense**, a free neon arcade defense/survival game, and AI has been a major part of the development workflow.

The important distinction for me is that I’m not just typing “make me a game” and accepting whatever comes back. I design the gameplay systems, decide how mechanics should interact, direct the visual style, test everything, reject bad implementations, and keep iterating until it feels right. AI helps me turn those ideas into working code and assets much faster than I could otherwise.

N3ONDefense is built around planting and defending bombsites while surviving increasingly aggressive enemy waves. It has procedural arenas, Mods that can completely change how abilities behave, mines, turrets, electric fences, bosses, progression, Overdrive difficulty, pickups, hazards, and a growing number of systems that interact with each other.

I’ve already reworked enemies multiple times, redesigned menus and UI, changed how mines function, rebuilt progression systems, tuned difficulty, improved procedural generation, and continued polishing anything that feels unfinished or unclear.

For me, AI is a development tool. The game design, direction, gameplay decisions, and overall experience are still mine.

I’d love to hear from other AI-assisted game developers about how you use AI in your own workflow, especially how much iteration you usually go through before something actually matches what you had in mind.

**N3ONDefense is free to play:** [n3ondefense.org](http://n3ondefense.org)
